references.text: God commands Noah to take seven pairs of every clean animal, which explains why he had clean animals available for burnt offerings after the flood.
Abel brings an animal offering from the firstborn of his flock to the Lord, the earliest example of a blood sacrifice that foreshadows Noah's burnt offering.
The Lord's response to Noah's offering – He smelled the pleasing aroma and promised never again to curse the ground because of humanity.
Abram builds an altar to the Lord at Shechem, continuing the pattern from Noah of building altars to worship God.
Abraham builds an altar and brings a burnt offering (the ram instead of Isaac), which recalls Noah's burnt offering.
Moses builds an altar under Mount Sinai, and young Israelites offer burnt offerings to the Lord, similar to Noah's altar-building and burnt offering.
Detailed legal regulations concerning the burnt offering in Leviticus 3, formalizing the type of sacrifice Noah brought spontaneously after the flood.
An exhortation to continually bring sacrifices of praise to God through Jesus Christ, which can be seen in light of Noah's gratitude expressed through his burnt offering.
A parallel between Noah and David, who both build altars and receive a response from God (fire) after offering burnt offerings.
Clear parallel: An offering on a self-built altar that turns God's judgment (flood/plague) into grace.
Thematic connection: The altar as the center of God's presence at the start of a new era (after the flood/construction of the temple).
Direct allusion to the same person (Noah) and event, even though the focus is on faith rather than sacrifice.
Narrative context: Noah's obedience before (7:5) and after (8:20) judgment.
Thematic parallel: Restoration of proper worship and an altar following a period of judgment/fall.
Connection through obedience in building an altar according to God's specific command.
Direct narrative link: Noah's total obedience (6:22) as the basis for the offering (8:20).
Clear parallel: An offering that triggers God's response and acceptance during a critical transitional period.
